title.es: Redactar una noticia breve y equilibrada

es: Redactar una noticia breve equilibrada: titular, lead con hechos, dos fuentes atribuidas, una cita y un grado de certeza marcado con una estructura impersonal.

teaching.en: The school fundraiser raised 1,200 euros for charity, the organiser said, and the proceeds will buy new books for the library.
teaching.es: El evento benéfico del colegio recaudó 1.200 euros para una organización benéfica, dijo la organizadora, y lo recaudado servirá para comprar libros nuevos para la biblioteca.
teaching.explanationEs: El lead da el hecho y su fuente: raised + cifra + said; fundraiser y proceeds pertenecen al mundo de la recaudación.
segments: The school fundraiser raised 1,200 euros for charity, the organiser said,
and the proceeds will buy new books for the library.
teaching.audioText: The school fundraiser raised 1,200 euros for charity, the organiser said, and the proceeds will buy new books for the library.

teaching.en: The turnout was higher than last year, according to the head teacher, although the final figure is still provisional.
teaching.es: La asistencia fue mayor que el año pasado, según la directora, aunque la cifra final todavía es provisional.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + fuente atribuye el dato; provisional avisa de que la cifra aún puede cambiar.
segments: The turnout was higher than last year, according to the
head teacher, although the final figure is still provisional.
teaching.audioText: The turnout was higher than last year, according to the head teacher, although the final figure is still provisional.

teaching.en: The school will confirm the date of the next fair on Monday, but some parents deny that the stalls were too expensive.
teaching.es: El colegio confirmará la fecha de la próxima feria el lunes, pero algunos padres niegan que los puestos fueran demasiado caros.
teaching.explanationEs: Confirm da un dato como seguro; deny + that recoge una negativa atribuida a alguien.
segments: The school will confirm the date of the next fair on
Monday, but some parents deny that the stalls were too expensive.
teaching.audioText: The school will confirm the date of the next fair on Monday, but some parents deny that the stalls were too expensive.

teaching.en: An impartial report attributes every important fact to a named source and keeps its own opinions out of the story.
teaching.es: Una noticia imparcial atribuye cada dato importante a una fuente con nombre y deja sus propias opiniones fuera de la historia.
teaching.explanationEs: Impartial = imparcial: sin adjetivos de elogio ni de crítica; las opiniones van entre comillas y atribuidas.
segments: An impartial report attributes every important fact to a named
source and keeps its own opinions out of the story.
teaching.audioText: An impartial report attributes every important fact to a named source and keeps its own opinions out of the story.

teaching.en: A direct quote, such as «It was the best fair ever» from one pupil, repeats exact words, whereas a paraphrase gives the same idea in the reporter's own words.
teaching.es: Una cita textual, como «It was the best fair ever» de un alumno, repite palabras exactas, mientras que una paráfrasis da la misma idea con las palabras del periodista.
teaching.explanationEs: Quote = cita entre comillas; paraphrase = misma idea con otras palabras, sin comillas.
segments: A direct quote, such as «It was the best fair ever» from one pupil, repeats
exact words, whereas a paraphrase gives the same idea in the reporter's own words.
teaching.audioText: A direct quote, such as «It was the best fair ever» from one pupil, repeats exact words, whereas a paraphrase gives the same idea in the reporter's own words.

teaching.en: The final figure is expected to reach 1,500 euros, which puts the fair among the most successful events in the history of the school.
teaching.es: Se espera que la cifra final llegue a 1.500 euros, lo que sitúa la feria entre los eventos más exitosos en la historia del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Is expected to + verbo base es la pasiva impersonal que marca un grado de certeza: probable, no confirmado.
segments: The final figure is expected to reach 1,500 euros, which puts the
fair among the most successful events in the history of the school.

prompt.es: Elige la frase de apertura (lead) más adecuada para una noticia imparcial.

choices.text: The amazing school fair raised a big 1,200 euros for charity on Saturday.
The school fair raised 1,200 euros for charity on Saturday, the organiser said.
The school fair will raise 1,200 euros for charity, according to some parents.

feedback.es: Da el hecho, la cifra y la fuente sin adjetivos de elogio; las otras opciones cargan la noticia de opinión o cambian la fuente y el tiempo.

hint.es: Busca la frase con hecho, cifra y fuente, sin adjetivos de elogio.

origin.text: Facts: the school fair raised 1,200 euros on Saturday for charity. The organiser gave the figure, and the final total has not been confirmed yet.

prompt.es: Completa: «La asistencia fue mayor que el año pasado, según la directora.»

feedback.es: According to + fuente atribuye el dato sin necesidad de un verbo de habla.

hint.es: La fuente se introduce con una expresión de dos palabras que termina en to.

origin.text: The turnout was higher than last year, ___ to the head teacher, who counted the visitors at the gate.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se espera confirmar la cifra final el lunes.»

answer.text: The final figure is expected to be confirmed on Monday

feedback.es: La pasiva impersonal is expected to be confirmed marca que la cifra es probable, no definitiva.

hint.es: Empieza por the final figure y usa is expected to be confirmed.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada parte de la noticia breve con su función.

pairs: School fair raises 1,200 euros for charity
The fair raised 1,200 euros on Saturday, the organiser said.
The total is expected to rise once all the donations are counted.
«It was the best fair ever,» said one pupil.

feedback.es: Una noticia breve combina un titular, un lead con fuente, una fórmula de cautela y una cita atribuida.

prompt.es: Escucha a la editora y elige qué corrección pide al borrador.

choices.text: To add more opinion words so that the brief sounds livelier.
To delete the figure because it does not matter to readers.
To remove the opinion words and attribute the figure to a named source.

feedback.es: Pide quitar «best» y «amazing» y nombrar a la organizadora como fuente de la cifra: tono neutral y dato atribuido.

origin.audio: An editor reads a draft aloud: the best fair in years raised an amazing 1,200 euros. She stops and says that the words best and amazing are opinions, and that there is no source for the figure. Add the organiser's name, she says, use the verb said, and keep the tone neutral.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se espera que confirme el total cuando se cuenten las donaciones.»

feedback.es: Confirm the total convierte una cifra provisional en un dato cerrado; la frase deja claro que todavía no ocurrió.

origin.text: The school has not announced a final figure yet. It is expected to ___ the total on Monday, once all the donations are counted.

prompt.es: Compara los dos borradores. ¿Por qué el segundo es más imparcial?

choices.text: It attributes each fact to a named source and avoids praise words.
It is longer and includes a direct quote from a pupil.
It describes the turnout without mentioning last year.

feedback.es: Nombra la fuente de cada dato (organizadora, directora) y elimina adjetivos como «amazing» o «big».

origin.text: Draft 1: The amazing school fair raised a big 1,200 euros, and everybody agrees that it was a great success. Draft 2: The school fair raised 1,200 euros for charity on Saturday, the organiser said. The turnout was higher than last year, according to the head teacher.

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión y elige qué pide la editora sobre la frase de los padres.

choices.text: To keep it, because every reader knows that it is true.
To name the source of the claim or remove it.
To turn it into a direct quote from the head teacher.

feedback.es: La frase no dice quiénes son los padres: la editora pide una fuente con nombre o eliminar la afirmación.

origin.audio: An editor reviews a draft about the school fair. She likes the lead, but she points out that the sentence about the parents has no source. Some parents may deny that the stalls were too expensive, she says, but the draft never says who they are. She suggests either naming one parent or removing the claim. Then she adds that the final figure is only provisional, so the draft should say that it is expected to reach fifteen hundred euros, not that it will reach it.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué pide escribir «expected to reach» la cifra.

choices.text: Because the organiser refused to give the figure.
Because the school wants readers to give more money.
Because the total is provisional and not yet confirmed.

feedback.es: La cifra final es provisional: is expected to reach refleja probabilidad, mientras que will reach afirmaría algo no confirmado.

prompt.es: Redacta la noticia breve con dos fuentes, una pasiva impersonal y una cita.

answer.text: School fair raises 1,500 euros for charity. The school fair raised 1,500 euros for a local children's charity on Saturday, the organiser said. The turnout was higher than last year, according to the head teacher, who added that more than four hundred people visited the stalls. The final figure is expected to be confirmed on Monday, when the last donations are counted. Some parents denied that the stalls were too expensive, and they described the atmosphere as friendly. «It was the best fair ever,» said one pupil. The school will announce the date of next year's fair in June, and volunteers are expected to meet in September to start planning. The event is believed to be the most successful fair in the school's history.
accepted: School fair raises 1,500 euros for charity. The school fair raised 1,500 euros for a local children's charity on Saturday, the organiser said. The turnout was higher than last year, according to the head teacher, who added that more than four hundred people visited the stalls. The final figure is expected to be confirmed on Monday, when the last donations are counted. Some parents denied that the stalls were too expensive, and they described the atmosphere as friendly. «It was the best fair ever,» said one pupil. The school will announce the date of next year's fair in June, and volunteers are expected to meet in September to start planning. The event is believed to be the most successful fair in the school's history.

Fair raises money for children's charity. St Mary's school raised 1,500 euros for a children's charity on Saturday, according to the organiser. The head teacher said that the turnout was higher than last year, with more than four hundred visitors. The final figure is expected to be confirmed on Monday. Some parents deny that the stalls were too expensive. «It was the best fair ever,» said one pupil. The fair is thought to be the most successful in the history of the school, and the date of the next one will be announced in June, so volunteers are expected to start planning in September.

feedback.es: Una buena noticia empieza por el hecho con su fuente, atribuye cada dato, marca la cautela con una pasiva impersonal y cita a un alumno con tono neutral.

origin.text: Notes: Saturday fair at St Mary's school; money for a children's charity. Organiser Laura Reed: 1,500 euros raised. Head teacher Mr Collins: turnout higher than last year, more than four hundred visitors, final figure to be confirmed on Monday. Some parents deny that the stalls were too expensive. One pupil said: «It was the best fair ever.»

prompt.es: Lee el comentario de la lectora. ¿Qué reprocha a la noticia?

choices.text: That a vague claim sounds firmer than the evidence shows.
That the brief contains a figure that is clearly false.
That the parents refused to speak to the reporter.

feedback.es: No dice que sea falsa: critica que «some parents» suene más firme de lo que permiten las pruebas, porque no se sabe cuántos padres hay detrás.

origin.text: Reader's comment: The brief says that some parents deny that the stalls were expensive, but it never says how many parents were asked. I am not saying that the brief is wrong, only that the claim sounds firmer than the evidence.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Algunos padres niegan que los puestos fueran demasiado caros.»

answer.text: Some parents deny that the stalls were too expensive

feedback.es: Deny that + oración recoge la negativa de los padres; el verbo de la subordinada va en pasado.

prompt.es: Completa: «La periodista decidió parafrasearlas en una frase más corta.»

feedback.es: Paraphrase es dar la misma idea con otras palabras, sin comillas, a diferencia de una cita textual.

origin.text: The reporter did not copy the head teacher's exact words: she chose to ___ them in a shorter sentence without quotes.
